item.title: Kukie Serving.07 API Gateway and Connector
item.description: How one public Kukie API address reaches models on customers’ own GPU clusters — Kotlin keeps accounts, permissions, keys and usage, a Go gateway relays JSON/SSE without storing bodies, and a connector inside each customer cluster dials out over WebSocket; plus the load test that moved key checks off the request path (member CPU 0.67 to 0.02 cores, ITL p95 72.5 to 29.3ms) and a 31-hour outage caused by credential re-issue.

item.title: Kukie Serving.06 Counter and Adaptive Limit
item.description: How kukie-counter, a Go proxy in front of vLLM, sets each model’s concurrency limit — first from the measured baseline × 0.8, then from the TTFT and ITL p95 it times on every stream (+1 / ×0.7 every 5 s) with a waiting-queue brake — and what two load tests on one L40S showed: 16 → 21 under SLA, a cascading cut on long prompts, and a 20 ms stall that lives in the proxy path, not in vLLM.

item.title: Network & K8s.04-3 Who May Knock
item.description: Having a path is not the same as being allowed to use it — a three-Pod lab (diagnostic, Go web server, PostgreSQL) shows what a NetworkPolicy really is: a per-Pod, per-direction allow list where both the sender’s egress door and the receiver’s ingress door must open, allow rules only add up, an empty selector, an empty list and an empty rule mean three different things, a hyphen in YAML decides AND versus OR, and the standard API stops at the TCP port while Cilium’s Envoy can refuse a single HTTP path with a 403.
